storyline.label: Diffusion Language
storyline.latest_title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents

prior_narrative.tldr: Diffusion language models first appeared here as the backbone of a tool-using chemistry agent. Days later they turned up on the offensive side, as a way to craft fluent black-box attacks on LLMs.
prior_narrative.whats_new: A new paper distills a decoding schedule so diffusion LLMs commit tokens in fewer rounds, targeting the parallel-generation speedup that has been hard to realize.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Diffusion LLMs only pay off for serving if parallel decoding cuts rounds without hurting quality; this is research-stage evidence, not a deployable runtime.

status.detail: Three arXiv papers, no production release: agents, attacks and decoding speed are each explored once.

beats.headline: Masked diffusion LMs drive a tool-integrated chemistry agent
Diffusion LMs used for perplexity-aware black-box attacks
Schedule distillation aims to cut dLLM decoding rounds

open_questions: Do the schedule-distillation speedups hold on independent benchmarks at equal output quality?
Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet; if you prototype one, measure decoding rounds and quality against your autoregressive baseline, and include fluent-prompt attacks in red-team evals.

day_captions.d4cd8af9958d846f: Shows a masked diffusion LM as the reasoning core of a tool-using chemistry agent.
day_captions.4d1cef01d9ab5673: Uses a diffusion LM to generate low-perplexity attack prompts against black-box LLMs.
day_captions.75e015095613159e: Proposes learning when to commit tokens, reducing the decoding rounds dLLMs need.
